archetypes.name: shell-set-e-invariants
archetypes.rationale: The driver pervasively toggles set +e/set -e around child calls; a missed re-enable or an early-exit path that bypasses _write_result_and_emit could silently drop the result env and trigger the mandatory-keys abort in the orchestrator.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review every `set +e` / `set -e` block in `skills/design/scripts/design-plan-quality-assessor.sh`. For each child invocation (`$SNAPSHOT_SH`, `$ASSESS_SH`, `append-tool-failure.sh`, `write-cursor` rollback), verify the exit code is captured before `set -e` is restored and that `_write_result_and_emit` is always reached on the settled exit-0 path. Check whether any failure mode (e.g., `append-tool-failure.sh` inside a `set +e` block that itself uses `rm -f`) can leave the script in a `set +e` state on the non-failure path. Also verify the SKILL.md Step 3.6 fence's outer `set +e` capture correctly restores `set -e` before the abort block. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: assess-round-regression
archetypes.rationale: assess-plan-round.sh had read_workflow_path renamed to resolve_workflow_path with new design_classification fallback logic; any callers or test fixtures that relied on the old function name or the old SIMPLE default would silently break.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the changes to `skills/design/scripts/assess-plan-round.sh`: the rename from `read_workflow_path` to `resolve_workflow_path` and the extraction of the `json_scalar_or_sed` helper. Grep for any remaining references to `read_workflow_path` in the repo. Check whether the new `design_classification` fallback (when `workflow_path` is empty, use `design_classification=HARD` to resolve `HARD`) matches the same fallback in `design-plan-quality-assessor.sh` and in the SKILL.md Step 3.6 fence — all three should agree. Also note that `json_scalar_or_sed` is now duplicated between `assess-plan-round.sh` and `design-plan-quality-assessor.sh`; verify both copies are byte-identical in behavior for the jq → sed fallback chain. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
